function: CNN estimates self-interference and UE channels from shared-pilot signals in full-duplex mmWave MIMO; FNN maps downlink-UE-to-RX-array channel to TX-array-to-UE channel (pp. 3, 7-9).
system: Single-cell full-duplex mmWave MIMO BS, separate 16-antenna TX and RX arrays, K=8 single-antenna UEs, 28 GHz, fully digital, 1-3 bit ADC cases; no RIS (pp. 4, 9).
method: Supervised CNN (0, 1, 2 or 10 hidden layers, 64 3x3 kernels) estimators and an FNN for RX-TX channel mapping; MSE loss, Adam, batch 512 (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: geometric UE channels (P=5 paths), Rician SI channel; 50,000 samples split 20,000/20,000/10,000; DeepMIMO O1 28 GHz used only for testing (pp. 4-5, 9, 13).
test_conditions: Trained on simulator channels; tested on 4977 DeepMIMO O1 28 GHz channels and over Rician factors 20-100 dB versus training kappa (pp. 11, 13-14).
baselines: Non-learned: LS and MMSE (empirical covariance, M=1000); learned: 10-hidden-layer CNN of [25] (DeepCNN) (pp. 3, 9, 11).
metrics: NMSE of SI and UE channels versus SNR, pilot dimension, hidden layers, ADC bits, correlation, kappa and angular spread; FLOPs (pp. 9-14).
complexity: FLOPs (Table 3, Fig. 18): MMSE quadratic in receive antennas, LS and CNN linear; each extra 64-kernel 3x3 layer adds about 1.5e8 FLOPs at 16 antennas (p. 14).
openness: none: no code or data link; DeepMIMO [31] public dataset used only for testing (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 9: "A dataset of 50, 000 samples is collected based on the channel model" (own geometric model of [32], path loss from [39], Rician SI channel, pp. 4-5); DeepMIMO appears only in the test phase (p. 13). Not trained on a standard or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "we utilize the DeepMIMO dataset in the test phase"; p. 14: "We generate 4977 channel realizations from the DeepMIMO dataset to test the NN model for UE channel estimation trained based on the channel data from geometrical channel models".
q3_support: p. 3: "compare them to traditional LS and MMSE techniques, as well as state-of-the-art deep NNs", with 10 hidden layers "corresponding to the deep NN architecture described in [25]"; p. 9: "NN-based channel estimator outperforms the LS and MMSE estimation"; NMSE compared in Fig. 5 (legend labels the 10-layer CNN [25]).
q4_support: p. 14: "we compare the computational complexity of the LS, MMSE, and NN channel estimators in terms of FLOPs"; Table 3 gives the FLOPs formulas, Fig. 18 the counts, and a hidden layer needs about 1.5e8 "more FLOPs for estimating a MIMO channel with 16 antennas".
q5_support: p. 13: "we utilize the DeepMIMO dataset in the test phase" only; training data come from the authors' own simulator (p. 9: "A dataset of 50, 000 samples is collected based on the channel model"); no code or data link or availability statement appears in the paper.
notes: Area 2: self-interference and UE channel estimation plus RX-TX channel mapping. q1 and q5 are 0 because training and all main results use the authors' simulator; the public DeepMIMO O1 28 GHz ray-tracing set appears only as a test set for distribution shift (pp. 13-14), so the reviewer may reconsider both. q3: the learned baseline is the 10-layer CNN of [25], which is also a depth variant inside the paper's own study; it is labelled [25] in Figs. 5, 6 and 8 and described as a state-of-the-art deep NN (p. 3).
